quests.title: Green Country
quests.description: Silverpine ends at a line you can see from the saddle: pine and blight on one side, barley on the other. Lordaeron fell and took its farmland with it, all but this valley. Aelin Frost has held the pass for two years and watched every courier stop dead at the top of the road to look at the colour of it.
quests.accept_text:
Everyone stops. I did. Two years dead and the first green I'd seen since, and I stood there like a fool.

Go down and get it over with. The square tower with our banner is Southpoint - Commander Rethven holds it, and she'll want to know what the pass road looks like behind you.
quests.turn_in_text: You stopped. Don't apologise for it. The day I meet someone who walks past that view without pausing is the day I stop trusting my own eyes.

quests.title: What Walks the Milestones
quests.description: Worgs on the pass road are ordinary. Worgs that work the same stretch at the same hour are not. Orlin has lost two couriers in a month, both on the run between the pass and the tower, both within an hour of dusk, and he has stopped calling it bad luck.
quests.accept_text:
They hunt the verges, so take the crown of the road and make them come out to you. Eight should do it - I'm not standing here counting for you.

And mark where they've been bedding. A worg that beds within sight of a road has stopped being a wolf. It's become a picket, and pickets get posted by something.
quests.turn_in_text: Bedded in sight of the milestones, all of them. So somebody's feeding them, or somebody's training them. Neither answer lets me sleep, and I don't sleep anyway.

quests.description: Southpoint's glue, lamp-oil, buttons and bowstring nocks come off the same animal. Dreng could requisition them through the Undercity, and the requisition would come back in the spring, correctly stamped, for half what he asked.
quests.accept_text:
Eight horns off the foothill rams and I'll have oil in the lamps by Thursday.

Understand what you're doing for me: I can write to Lordaeron and be answered in April, or I can send you up a hill. The Dark Lady gave us our freedom. Nobody thought to give us a supply line.
quests.turn_in_text: Eight, and two matched. Signed for and counted twice, which means you're in my ledger now. That's a better place to be than most places in this valley.

quests.title: Something Living
quests.description: Four years Jessel Vane has worked blighted earth, because blighted earth is what Tirisfal has. Then he crossed a ridge and found soil with roots in it. He has not said so to the Commander, but he has begun taking samples before anyone upriver decides green farmland is a problem that needs solving.
quests.accept_text:
Six jars, six different fields, kept apart - the difference between them is the entire point, so don't fill all six from the nearest ditch. I'll know.

And since you're not from here: what does soil smell like where you're from? Not a joke. I've been trying to remember what it's supposed to smell like and I find I can't, and I'd rather ask someone who hasn't had the chance to forget.
quests.turn_in_text:
Living. All six. Roots, mites, the lot.

You said yours smelled like rain on stone. I'm going to think about that for a while.

quests.title: The Militia Question
quests.description: Twice a week Hillsbrad's militia walk up the tower road, stand at a respectful distance, look at Southpoint, and walk away. Rethven's orders say hold the tower. They say nothing about men who come to count her walls and never once draw.
quests.accept_text:
Ten of them, in the fields, and I want you to understand I've thought about this longer than it sounds.

They're farmers with billhooks and a grievance, and the grievance is fair - we are standing in their valley. But they've been measuring my gate for a month, and men who measure a gate are deciding something. I'd rather they decided it with ten fewer.

quests.title: Billhook and Halberd
quests.description: Sarra Dunwick's whole trade is knowing what a valley is doing before the valley announces it. What this one is doing is arming the people who bring in the barley, and calling it a harvest watch.
quests.accept_text:
Ten, out in the rows. But I don't want the count - I want what's in their hands when they go down.

A billhook is a tool a frightened man picks up. A halberd is a thing somebody made, carried to a field, and put into his hands on purpose. If you find halberds out there, this stopped being a harvest watch before either of us arrived.
quests.turn_in_text:
Halberds. Six of ten.

Someone is arming this valley and it isn't Southshore's garrison - they'd keep the good steel for marines. That leaves a quartermaster with a grudge, or Alterac money. I'll find out.

quests.accept_text:
You've got hands and you've got a bench. Five batches of rough shafts and we'll call the ram I owe you square.

I'll tell you what I tell the Marshal: my grandfather took rams off that hill when Alterac still had a king, and nobody's shown me the paper that changed it. They dissolved a whole kingdom up there and never once came down here to say who owns the sheep.

quests.title: Off the Snowline
quests.description: Maud Kellen has read weather off her animals for thirty years. Her rams have been bunching at the low fence for a week and refusing the top pasture, which means the yetis have come down early, which means the snowline has moved and the winter is going to be a bad one.
quests.accept_text:
Six, up where the grass goes thin, and go in daylight.

I'll say this plain, because I've been told what you are: they tell me you get back up. If that's true then you can walk a gully I'd not send my own son up, and I'd be a liar if I said that didn't sit strange with me. Take the work anyway. I need the pasture more than I need to be comfortable about it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Rams spread back out by evening. That's how I know you did it, not because you said so.

And you came back down the gully on your own feet. I notice that too.

Take the cloak off the peg by the door before you go. It was my husband's and it's seen that gully before.

quests.accept_text:
He drills them in open ground where anyone can see, which is arrogance. He won't break and run, which isn't.

I'd rather fight one officer than the hundred farmers he's six months from making. That's the whole of my reasoning and I'd say it to his face.
quests.turn_in_text:
He swore on the soil, they tell me. That's the oath the militia take here - not to a king, there isn't one left, but to the ground.

The ground kept its half. It usually does.

quests.description: Nols has counted the Daggerspine on the western strand for three weeks. The count goes up every week. Murlocs do not breed that fast, which means they are not breeding - they are arriving, and he would like to know what from.

Ten off the shingle, and while you're down there keep half an eye on the water behind them.

They come up the beach facing inland. Every one of them. Whatever they're running from is seaward, and I've been watching that water for three weeks and it has never once looked back at me.
quests.turn_in_text:
Ten down, and the count's still rising.

That's the answer, and it's the one I didn't want. They aren't taking the strand. They're being pushed onto it.

That's the Maiden's Grace. That's my ship, and that's Harl's hand it came off, because he was the only one of us with fingers fat enough to need it cut.

Keep it. I've looked at that water for a month. I don't need something to hold while I do it.

I'm walking inland in the morning. Thirty-one years at sea and I'm going to go and look at a field. Don't follow me and don't wave.

Ten in among the rows, and keep your chin tucked - they go for the eyes and they're clever about it.

Every orchard between here and Lordaeron is ash or worse. This one came through. I'm not losing it to insects after it survived the end of a kingdom.

Go unarmed and look poor. And be clear with yourself before you set off: if they take you, nobody is coming. I'll write it up as a loss and move my camp.

Then we aren't taking Southshore this year, nor next. I'll send that north and someone in the Undercity will be disappointed in a way that doesn't reach us. Good.

East, the whole length of it. You'll know Tarren Mill when you see the wheel - there's a mill on a diverted race and the race cuts the town clean in two. Report to Magistrate Pell at the gate.

Sixty years that wheel's turned. Lordaeron fell, the Scourge came through, the valley changed hands twice, and nobody on either side ever thought to stop the wheel.

When you get there, mind the race. It's a cut channel, it's deep the whole way, and there are three bridges and no fourth. People try the water about twice a year and the wheel gives them back about a week later.

You made it. I had you as a maker - boots were right and you looked at the treeline instead of the road.

quests.description: The Syndicate have stopped robbing the eastern roads and started owning them. Kolt does not much mind robbery - robbery is weather. Ten, off the eastern roads. Violet sashes, and nothing they carry has a maker's mark on it - they file them off, every piece.

Take the sashes if you want my thanks in writing. The colour's Alterac's. They've no kingdom to wear it for and they've kept wearing it anyway, which tells you what we're dealing with better than I can.

quests.description: Ovid Thane runs the carts - flour west out of Tarren Mill, reagents back east - twice a month without fail for six years. The last two runs west did not arrive. Four sacks, sealed with my mark, and they go on your back rather than on an axle. West road all the way to the forward post in the fields - ask for Ivek, he's expecting a cart and he'll be delighted.

Don't set it down. Not to rest, not to fight, not for anything. A sealed consignment that touches the ground is a consignment somebody can swear was opened.

My mark, unbroken, and Ivek's countersign. First flour to reach the fields in two months.

I'm going to send the next one the same way and let the carts go out empty as bait.

quests.description: Dell Varrow was gamekeeper on this land when it had a lord worth keeping game for. He knows every hedgerow between the mill and the hollow, which is how he knows that every one of them currently has something living in it that did not use to.

They run in threes. That's not a rule of thumb, it's how they're built - one shows itself, one circles, one waits. If you've found one you've found three, and the third is behind you. Count to three before you swing and you'll be fine.

Eight. And you counted before you swung - I could tell from how few of them got round you.

quests.title: Uphill of the Vats
quests.description: Field Apothecary Wren samples the ditches east of the mill so the apothecaries inside the walls do not have to. So it isn't us. Which means I have to go and tell the Society that something else is in this water, and they are going to be very disappointed in me for being right.

They left the STAKES. Do you understand what that means? They didn't miss them. They pulled the line, coiled the wire, and left me the bits I'd have to dig out. That's not scavenging.

Ten. Good.

I've been doing this eleven years and I've never once been mocked by the wildlife. I'd like it on record that I'm handling it well.

You'll have seen a lot of new things since you came to this world. That wall was old when Lordaeron was founded. It was old when Alterac was founded. Everything you've watched fall this year was built in its shadow.

An empire falls, then the kingdoms it made fall, and the wall outlives all of them without a garrison. There's a lesson in that and I have never once enjoyed it.

quests.title: Iron for the Spindle
quests.description: Aldous Reed's family has milled here sixty years. In that time Lordaeron fell, the valley changed hands twice, and the dead took the east bank - and the wheel has not stopped for any of it. The spindle bands have, however, started to go, and a spindle band is not something you improvise.

objectives.label: Smelt iron bars for the spindle bands

quests.accept_text:
Four bars of iron, smelted proper. Not bronze - I know what bronze does in a wet bearing and so will you after one winter.

Sixty years that wheel's turned. My grandfather kept it going through the Second War by swapping the bands out himself. I'd not like to be the Reed who let it stop over four bars of iron.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four, and good ones.

She'll turn another sixty on these. I'll not be here for it, but she will, and that's the arrangement we've always had.

quests.description: Mallory Dunn feeds both banks, which is a diplomatic position she never asked for and handles by not asking anybody which side they came off. The problem with feeding both banks is that one half of her custom eats and the other half watches, and the half that eats has opinions about mutton.
quests.accept_text:
Six good haunches off the foothill rams, west past the Foothills. Ram, mind, not sheep - there's a difference and this room will tell me about it for a week.

And take the west road, not the hollow. I've lost two suppliers to that hollow and I'd rather keep the one who can carry six.
quests.turn_in_text:
Six, and hung properly. You've done this before.

Room's yours tonight and I'll not ask which bank you'd rather drink on. Nobody asks that in my house.

quests.title: Charcoal, Not Coal
quests.description: Odrin Vance shoes the Society's horses and mends their cart axles and takes their money, and has stopped apologising for it to anyone who asks. A trade is a trade. What he will not do is burn the coal they keep offering him, because coal is wrong for fine work and always has been.
quests.accept_text:
Six oakheart planks, cut and seasoned at a sawmill. I'll burn my own charcoal from them - it's the only way I'll know what went into it.

They keep sending me coal from Dun Garok's old workings. Cheaper, hotter, and it ruins a weld - you get a seam that looks perfect and opens in a year. I'll not put my mark on that for anybody's convenience.
quests.turn_in_text:
Oakheart, properly seasoned. I can tell by the weight before I've even split one.

That's a season of good work in the stack. And when the next cart of coal turns up, I'll have somewhere to point.

quests.title: Yew from the River Stand
quests.description: Tess Aldren strings bows the way her father strung them, which means yew off the river stand and nothing else. The river stand is three miles out past the hedgerows and the hedgerows currently have worgs in them, which has made a familiar errand into an annual one.
quests.accept_text:
The gnolls have been felling the river stand for den stakes. Six staves back off them - and look at the cut before you pick one up. Heartwood and sapwood both, or it's firewood and I'll say so.

My father cut there, and his father. There's a mark on one of those trunks that's four generations of us deep. They're burning it to hold up a roof made of my snare wire.
quests.turn_in_text:
All six true, and every one of them off the right side of the trunk.

Four generations of doing it one way, and a gnoll nearly ended it for kindling. I'll string the first tonight.

quests.title: Label Everything
quests.description: Nilla Stitch labels every jar in the apothecarium, which is not the junior work it sounds like. A consignment came in from Gavin's Naze last month with half the labels soaked off in transit, and nobody in the building is willing to open an unmarked jar to find out what is in it.
quests.accept_text:
Seven unmarked jars went out with the Naze consignment before anyone noticed. I need them back, and I need them back closed.

I'm aware how this sounds. But the whole discipline is that you know what you're holding. An unlabelled jar in a Syndicate camp is somebody's accident waiting to be somebody else's epidemic.
quests.turn_in_text:
Seven, all closed, none of them opened.

You've no idea what a good day this is. I'll have them catalogued by morning and nobody will ever know they left.

quests.title: The Chapel on the West Bank
quests.description: There is a chapel on the west bank and a living chaplain in it, in a town held by the Forsaken. Ewen Blackwood has never been told to stop and has never asked why. He buries the village's dead in ground the Society could want, and so far nobody has wanted it.
quests.accept_text:
Six markers went missing out of the yard - stone ones, with names cut in them. Syndicate, most likely; cut stone sells.

I'll say the thing nobody here says to you. You die and you get up again, and the people in my yard do not. I've no quarrel with you for it. But you'll understand why a man in my trade thinks about it when you walk past.
quests.turn_in_text:
Six names back in the ground where they were put.

That's all a marker is - a promise that somebody stays where they were laid. It's the only promise I've got left to keep and I'd rather keep it.

quests.title: Reagents from the Hollow
quests.description: Lysbet Crane's vats run on things that have to be gathered rather than bought, and the Mudsnout gnolls have taken the hollow where most of them grow. She would rather send someone than explain to the Society why a quarter's work stalled over fungus.
quests.accept_text:
Eight bloodcaps, out of the wet ground in Mudsnout Hollow. They grow where the water sits.

Cut them, don't pull them - the whole value is in the stem and you'll crush it if you're rough. And don't eat one on a dare. I've had that conversation twice and one of those people is still here, after a fashion.
quests.turn_in_text:
Eight, cut clean. That's a quarter's work secured and one fewer letter I have to write.

Mind the vats on your way out. What's in them isn't finished and it doesn't like being looked at.

quests.title: Stir It, Skim It, Log It
quests.description: Grusk tends the vats on the east bank and considers it the best thing to have happened to him since dying. The work needs a reagent the Society sources from Durnholde's undercroft, which has become difficult since the Syndicate started keeping the keep properly.
quests.accept_text:
Eight of their binders, inside the keep.

The Society used to send a cart to the undercroft twice a year and nobody minded. Now there are wizards on the gate. Twelve years dead and I've got a trade again - stir it, skim it, log it - and I'm not losing it because Alterac's leftovers found religion.
quests.turn_in_text:
Eight. The cart can go out again.

You'll not understand what that's worth. I was a cooper before. I'm a vat-tender now. It's near enough the same job and it's the only thing that is.

quests.title: Horses Won't Cross at Night
quests.description: Brann Teague's horses will not cross the bridges after dark. He has tried leading them, blindfolding them and bribing them. They cross all day without complaint and refuse from dusk, and the only thing that has changed is the number of worgs working the hedgerows on the far side.
quests.accept_text:
Eight out of the hedges east of the race. Then I'll try the bridge at dusk again and we'll see.

Horses are clever animals and they're not clever in the way people think. They don't reason it out. They just know, and they're right more often than the men leading them.
quests.turn_in_text:
Led a pair across at last light with no trouble at all.

So it was the worgs. I'd rather it was the worgs than the other thing I'd started wondering about.

quests.title: Shoes for the Carts
quests.description: Nell Marsh keeps half the town moving - hooves and hinges, as she puts it. The caravan runs west twice a month and the last two came back with the draught team lame, which she traced to shoes cut from the cheap bronze stock the Society bought in bulk.

objectives.label: Forge a set of heavy bronze plate

quests.accept_text:
Two sets of heavy bronze at the forge, and I'll cut the shoe stock off them myself - the plate's the right thickness and the Society's bar stock isn't.

I know it's a strange way round. I'd rather ruin good plate than put another cart team lame on the west road.
quests.turn_in_text:
Right thickness, right temper. I'll have the team shod by the week's end.

And next time somebody buys bar stock by weight instead of by trade, I'll be shown the invoice first.

quests.title: A Government With No Country
quests.description: Vellis Thorne holds the middle of a valley with Alterac at her back and Southshore at her front, and of the two she loses more sleep over Alterac. Southshore is a garrison and behaves like one. The Syndicate is a dissolved kingdom's nobility with money, grudges and fifteen years of practice.
quests.accept_text:
Ten of their binders, wherever you find them east of the mill.

Understand what they are. Alterac let the Horde through the pass in the Second War and the Alliance dissolved the kingdom for it. The lords went into these hills with their titles and no land. They are not bandits. They're a court in exile, and courts in exile want their country back.
quests.turn_in_text:
Ten.

They'll replace them. That's the thing about a court - there's always another son. But it buys me a season, and a season in this valley is a long time.

quests.title: Eyes on Durnholde
quests.description: Mirren Vask walks the roads so the garrison does not have to guess. Durnholde is the one place he has never been able to report on properly, because the Syndicate hold the walls and he has only ever seen the keep from the bluff.
quests.accept_text:
Through the fallen archway and into the gatehouse ground. Far enough to count what's standing. Not far enough to be counted yourself.

The keep is a ring - outer wall, inner keep, and a courtyard between them. If the inner keep is still sealed, they're holding it properly and we need a plan. If it's open, they're squatting and we need a day.
quests.turn_in_text:
Sealed. Of course it's sealed.

They've been in there fifteen years and they've kept the inner keep shut the whole time. That's not squatting. That's a garrison, and I'll report it as one.

quests.title: The Fissure Above the Naze
quests.description: Gavin's Naze is the Alterac road and the Syndicate's front door, and the Roadwarden knows every track off it. Three years ago a fissure opened in the foothills north of the Naze, in ground that three kingdoms had surveyed and none of them had found anything in. Blood elves have been using it as a supply road for most of that time.
quests.accept_text:
Eight of the Syndicate off the north track first - they have been sitting on that road watching the elves come and go and taking a tithe, and I would like the road clear before I send anybody up it.

Then go up to the mouth itself and look down it. Do not go in. I have had two men offer and I have told both of them no, and I will tell you the same until somebody can tell me what is at the bottom.
quests.turn_in_text:
Cold air coming up out of it in the middle of summer, and a road worn into the lip.

Worn, you said. That takes years of boots. They have been going up and down that hole since it opened and nobody on this side has asked them what for.

quests.description: The card is oiled linen, folded small, and the Syndicate bandit you took it from had it sewn inside a cuff. One side is a sketch of the Alterac foothills with the fissure marked. The other is a list of times - arrivals and departures at the mouth, kept nightly, in a careful hand, for four months.
quests.accept_text:
Somebody paid the Syndicate to count blood elves going into a hole in the ground, and the Syndicate did it properly for four months.

Six more tallies off their couriers on the Naze road. Whoever commissioned this was not after the elves - you do not need four months of arrivals to rob a column. You need four months of arrivals to work out what is down there and how much of it there is.
quests.turn_in_text:
Six tallies, six hands, one ledger - and not one of those hands is Syndicate.

They were counting for somebody else. I do this work for a living and I did not know anyone else was doing it on my road.

quests.title: A Matter of Impossibility
quests.description:
Apothecary Lydon has spent eleven years on Alterac yeti and considers himself the authority, which he is, because nobody else wanted it.

A caravan master came through Tarren Mill with a story about yeti on the other side of the world, in a desert province of Kalimdor, and Lydon has been unable to put it down. Yeti do not cross oceans. The caravan master was very sure.

objectives.label: Deliver the sealed query to Elder Mura Longstand

quests.accept_text:
I am not asking you to believe it. I am asking you to carry this across an ocean and put it in the hand of whoever is senior at that camp, and let them tell me I am wasting my time.

It is sealed. Do not open it. The questions in it are embarrassing and I would like them answered before they are laughed at.
quests.turn_in_text:
He writes a very careful letter for a man who has already decided.

Tell him yes. Tell him there are yeti in this mountain and we would all be happier if there were not.
